articles.title: NASA publishes images of the location on the Moon where the SpaceX rocket impacted
articles.standfirst: The space agency confirms the creation of a new crater
articles.summary: The space agency confirms the creation of a new crater
articles.body:
The NASA has released new images of the Moon's surface showing the crater formed after the impact of a Falcon 9 rocket from SpaceX . Although the launch took place in January 2025, it was not until last August 5 of this year that the collision occurred and the crater was consequently created.

“Thanks to the variety of viewing angles, scientists were able to see the crater under various lighting conditions that revealed unique features. In the images where the crater rim stood out, they measured its width at 18 meters (60 feet). They also determined that the crater is less than three meters (10 feet) deep based on the length of its shadow,” NASA explains on its website.

Maximum precision for capturing the impact images

To capture images of the impact, engineers tilted the spacecraft so that its cameras pointed toward the crater each time the LRO passed about 96 kilometers (60 miles) above the Moon, traveling at an approximate speed of 1.6 kilometers per second (one mile per second).

“Getting the orientation right was only half the challenge; the timing also had to be precise. If the camera captured the image just 10 seconds too early or too late, the target would be 16 kilometers (10 miles) off from its central position.”, NASA notes.

To capture these details, LRO used its Narrow Angle Camera, which can detect features as small as 90 centimeters (three feet) wide.

Thanks to this study, NASA has been able to verify that “the lighter bands near the edge of the crater are made of fresh material excavated from deeper in the subsurface.”

In the released images, some darker areas can be seen that correspond to dust and rocks from the surface itself. Meanwhile, the brighter areas are composed of “more recent material that had remained buried at greater depth and was exposed after the collision”.

articles.title: Father leaves 7-year-old son alone on Mount Fuji and tells him to wait eight hours
articles.standfirst: The exhausted child was found sitting alone nearly 8,200 feet up the mountain with only snacks and a soft drink while his father continued climbing with his older brother
articles.summary: The exhausted child was found sitting alone nearly 8,200 feet up the mountain with only snacks and a soft drink while his father continued climbing with his older brother
articles.body:
A seven-year-old boy told his father he was tired while climbing Mount Fuji. What happened next has stunned people across Japan.

Instead of ending the climb or staying with his exhausted son, the 48-year-old father reportedly left the boy alone near the sixth station of the Fujinomiya Trail and continued up the mountain with his older son .

The instruction he allegedly gave the seven-year-old before leaving made the situation even more difficult to understand: wait there for around eight hours.

The child was eventually found sitting alone on a bench near a mountain hut at an altitude of roughly 2,500 meters nearly 8,200 feet with his father nowhere in sight.

Seven-year-old had no money and little food

A mountain hut worker noticed the boy alone shortly after 7 a.m. on Thursday, August 20.

According to Japanese media reports, the child appeared tired and explained that his father had gone on ahead. He reportedly had only some snacks and a soft drink with him and did not have any money.

Although the boy had appropriate climbing equipment, mountain hut staff became concerned and brought him to safety before contacting police.

The situation was particularly concerning because conditions on Mount Fuji can change quickly. Rain was falling and fog was developing around the mountain that morning, potentially making visibility and conditions more difficult.

Police began trying to locate the father and discovered that he had continued climbing with the boy's older brother, a first-year middle school student. By then, they had reached around the eighth station.

Police ordered the father to come back

Officers contacted the father and instructed him to abandon the climb and return to his younger son .

The family was finally reunited around noon, more than five hours after the mountain hut worker first noticed the boy alone. Fortunately, the seven-year-old was not injured.

But police reportedly gave his father a stern warning over the decision to leave such a young child behind. According to TV Asahi, authorities told him his actions could potentially violate the law and made another point especially clear: a mountain hut is not a daycare center.

The father reportedly showed remorse over what had happened.

The incident has since generated strong reactions in Japan, but it has also become a reminder of one of the simplest rules of hiking in a group: reaching the summit should never become more important than the people climbing with you.

Police urged hikers to plan around the person with the least stamina in their group and to make sure no one becomes separated.

For a seven-year-old who had already said he was too tired to continue, that would have meant something very simple. The climb should have ended there.

articles.title: Ancient mystery solved as missing half of colossal Ramesses II statue returns after 94 years
articles.standfirst: Archaeologists found the long-lost piece buried beneath the ground, allowing a 40-ton monument to stand complete again more than 3,000 years after it was created
articles.summary: Archaeologists found the long-lost piece buried beneath the ground, allowing a 40-ton monument to stand complete again more than 3,000 years after it was created
articles.body:
In 1930, German archaeologist Günther Roeder uncovered the lower portion of an enormous statue of Ramesses II at El-Ashmunein in Egypt's Minya Governorate. The discovery immediately suggested that the complete monument must once have been colossal.

But there was an obvious problem. The rest of the pharaoh was missing.

For the next 94 years, the upper half remained hidden until an Egyptian-American archaeological team made the discovery researchers had been waiting decades for. It was still there, buried beneath the ancient city.

Archaeologists found the missing half of Ramesses II

The breakthrough came in February 2024 during excavations carried out by a joint mission from Egypt's Supreme Council of Antiquities and the University of Colorado Boulder.

Researchers uncovered the upper section of a massive limestone statue measuring approximately 3.7 meters, or 12 feet, tall and weighing around 12 tons. The figure showed Ramesses II seated, wearing the double crown and a headdress decorated with a royal cobra.

But finding a giant piece of an ancient statue didn't automatically mean researchers had solved the mystery. They still needed to prove it belonged to the lower section discovered in 1930.

Archaeological and technical studies eventually confirmed exactly that: after 94 years apart, researchers had found the missing half.

The discovery became even more remarkable when archaeologists examined its condition. Despite spending centuries underground, traces of ancient color remained on parts of the statue, offering researchers a rare glimpse of how the monument may once have appeared.

The two halves finally came back together

Finding the missing piece was only the beginning. Researchers carried out extensive digital documentation, conservation assessments and structural studies to determine whether the enormous sections could safely be reunited.

The challenge was significant. The upper portion alone weighed approximately 12 tons, while the foundations beneath the statue also required stabilization.

After Egypt's Permanent Committee for Ancient Egyptian Antiquities approved the restoration plan, work began in September 2025. Nearly a century after the lower half was discovered, the two sections were finally brought back together.

In February 2026, Egyptian authorities announced that the restoration and reinstallation had been completed. The result is enormous.

The restored limestone statue stands approximately 6.7 meters about 22 feet tall and weighs more than 40 tons. And archaeologists didn't simply put it back together.

They returned Ramesses II to the place where the statue originally stood: in front of the northern entrance of the ancient temple at El-Ashmunein.

Ramesses II stands again thousands of years later

El-Ashmunein was known in antiquity as Khemnu and later as Hermopolis Magna , an important religious and administrative center in Middle Egypt.

Ramesses II ruled Egypt for more than six decades during the 19th Dynasty and became one of the most recognizable pharaohs in history. His reign left behind temples, inscriptions and monumental statues across Egypt.

The El-Ashmunein colossus is now another extraordinary survivor of that legacy.

Its return also required far more than simply placing one giant stone on top of another. Specialists studied the weight of the monument, the condition of its limestone, the stability of its foundations and the alignment of the massive blocks before reconstruction could be completed.

The restored statue now weighs more than 40 tons and once again presents the ancient king seated before the temple entrance.

The archaeological work at El-Ashmunein isn't finished either. The Egyptian-American mission, which has been working at the site since 2023, continues studying and excavating the ancient city.

That means the ground surrounding Ramesses II may still have more secrets to reveal. But one mystery that began with Roeder's discovery in 1930 has finally been solved.

The archaeologists who uncovered the lower half never got to see the complete monument. Nearly a century later, we finally can.

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet floods leave nearly 100 dead and hundreds missing
articles.summary: A sudden flood hit Nepal and the Tibet border region early Wednesday, killing more than 100 people and leaving hundreds missing, including more than 300 foreign tourists.
articles.body:
A sudden flood hit Nepal and the Tibet border region early Wednesday, killing more than 100 people and leaving hundreds missing, including more than 300 foreign tourists.

Authorities reported deaths across several districts north and west of Kathmandu, while local officials warned the toll could rise as the scale of the destruction becomes clearer.

Most of the missing tourists were reportedly near Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar in Tibet, a sacred site for several religions where a festival is scheduled to take place this week.

articles.title: Who is María Vargas, the new Miss Universe Mexico 2026 who succeeds Fátima Bosch?
articles.standfirst: She received the title from Fátima Bosch in the final held in Los Cabos
articles.summary: She received the title from Fátima Bosch in the final held in Los Cabos
articles.body:
María Vargas is the new Miss Universe Mexico . On the night of August 29, at Rancho Tierra Sagrada in Los Cabos, the representative of Jalisco prevailed among 32 candidates and received the crown from Fátima Bosch , who concluded a year of reign.

Vargas, 28, comes to the title with a profile that combines experience as a model, academic training, and personal projects. She holds a degree in International Business, has worked as a writer, and is the author of the book Miss Trouble , in which she addresses the criticism and judgment she faced throughout her career.

Jalisco's triumph and the winner's profile

From the early stages of the pageant, María Vargas positioned herself among the favorites. Her performance in the competitions, command of the stage, and a speech focused on women's identity and the ability to leave a mark established her as one of the strongest contenders.

The result sparked celebration in Jalisco, a state that adds a new national crown. Vargas not only brought the name of her state to the main stage, but now also assumes the responsibility of representing Mexico on the international stage with a message of self-definition and personal strength.

The final brought together one candidate from each state and was decided with the support of the jury and the public. The announcement of her name closed the evening and immediately opened the preparation stage on the road to Miss Universe.

María Vargas, Fátima Bosch's successor

Fátima Bosch handed over the crown after a year of public activities, promotion, and national and international representation. The woman from Tabasco concluded her term with an intense schedule and now yields the place to Vargas, who will have to assume the role of spokesperson in social projects and official events.

The title demands constant preparation: languages, media handling, presence in public forums, and intensive training in the face of global competition. The new queen has just over two months to refine every detail before traveling to Puerto Rico.

Maria Vargas takes over with the support of her state and a profile that combines personal trajectory and public projection. The road to Miss Universe 2026 has already begun.

Mexico will have in Puerto Rico a representative who arrives with her own voice and with the responsibility of maintaining the country's presence in the competition's most important pageant.

articles.title: Who is Sarah Khalifa? The famous Egyptian presenter sentenced to hang for her involvement in drug trafficking
articles.standfirst: Egyptian TV star faces death sentence in major drug trafficking case
articles.summary: Egyptian TV star faces death sentence in major drug trafficking case
articles.body:
Sarah Khalifa is a 39-year-old Egyptian television presenter whose career has taken a dramatic turn after she was sentenced to death in a major drug trafficking case.

Khalifa became known to Egyptian audiences through “Mission Impossible,” a television programme focused on security and crime.

She also built a substantial presence away from television, reportedly running a cosmetic surgery clinic and an event planning company. Her social media following has grown to more than two million Instagram users.

A Cairo Criminal Court sentenced Khalifa and 11 other defendants to death by hanging on September 5, 2026, after finding them guilty in a sprawling case involving the manufacture and trafficking of synthetic narcotics.

The case involved 28 defendants in total, with prosecutors alleging that the group had divided responsibilities between importing raw materials, manufacturing drugs and distributing them.

Authorities reportedly seized more than 750 kilograms of narcotics and materials used in their production. Investigators also found two residential apartments that were allegedly being used as laboratories, along with unlicensed firearms and ammunition.

Prosecutors said evidence against the defendants included witness statements as well as technical and digital material, including messages, photographs and videos.

What did Sarah Khalifa say about the allegations?

Khalifa has strongly denied being involved in the alleged criminal operation. During the investigation and court proceedings, she maintained that she was innocent and rejected the accusations against her.

“Please listen to me, sir. My parents raised me well; they are people who pray, and I don’t need drug money,” Khalifa told officials.

Egyptian media reported that she became emotional when the death sentence was announced and appealed to the court to listen to her defence.

She also reportedly told investigators that she’d never smoked a cigarette in her life. In court, she questioned why she would need money from drugs and referred to her parents and their religious upbringing while pleading her case.

Khalifa was arrested in Cairo in April 2025 as authorities investigated the alleged network. Prosecutors have claimed that the organization imported substances from abroad for the production of synthetic drugs and operated from residential premises.

Two other suspects reportedly remain at large and have been placed on travel restrictions and watch lists.

The death sentence isn't necessarily the end of the legal process. Egyptian law requires death sentences to be referred to the country's Grand Mufti for an advisory religious opinion, which the court received before confirming the verdict. The defendants can appeal through the Court of Cassation.

Nine other defendants in the case were sentenced to life imprisonment, while seven were acquitted. Khalifa also received a separate three-year prison sentence in another case concerning the assault and filming of her driver.

Egypt permits the death penalty for serious offences including drug trafficking, terrorism and premeditated murder.

articles.title: China's Great Green Wall could cover 88 million acres, but scientists warn it may not be enough
articles.standfirst: Decades of restoration have pushed back desertification, but preserving those gains remains a huge challenge.
articles.summary: Decades of restoration have pushed back desertification, but preserving those gains remains a huge challenge.
articles.body:
China has spent nearly half a century building one of the world's most ambitious environmental projects, creating a vast "Great Green Wall" intended to stop deserts swallowing productive land.

Officially known as the Three North Protective Forest Program , the project began in 1978 and is scheduled to continue until 2050.

By then, it is expected to encompass roughly 88 million acres of forest across northern China.

The results so far are significant. Government figures cited by The Independent indicate that forests planted through the program cover a cumulative 500,000 square kilometers, while China's desertified land has shrunk by around 10 percent overall since 2000.

"The broad significance of the Three-North Program is not only the scale of restoration, but the long-term political commitment behind it," Barron Joseph Orr , chief scientist for the U.N. Convention to Combat Desertification, said.

China's Great Green Wall has transformed huge areas

Forest cover across the program area increased from about 5 percent in 1978 to 14 percent in 2022.

Scientists have also recorded a decline of more than 40 percent in areas classified as severely or extremely desertified.

But Zhu Jiaojun of the Chinese Academy of Sciences warned that human intervention isn't the only reason conditions have improved.

"The achievement of desertification combat is due to people's hard work and a bit of luck with climate," Zhu said.

Increased rainfall in some regions has helped vegetation recover, while millions of workers have planted trees, maintained irrigation systems and built straw checkerboards designed to stabilize shifting sand.

Scientists warn the work can't simply stop

The bigger concern is whether those improvements can survive without decades more investment and maintenance.

Restored dryland ecosystems can eventually become more self-sustaining, but water availability, soil quality and careful monitoring remain crucial.

Zhu said the central question is what happens if the enormous level of human intervention is eventually reduced.

"This is what we are very concerned with and this is also the biggest challenge," he said.

China's experience also shows why planting trees alone isn't a global solution to desertification.

Africa's separate Great Green Wall project has restored millions of hectares, but funding shortages, political instability and extreme weather have slowed progress dramatically.

China has demonstrated that large scale restoration is possible.

What scientists aren't yet convinced of is whether those gains can endure without generations more work.

articles.title: The planets would not orbit exactly around the Sun
articles.standfirst: Our star doesn't remain completely still either
articles.summary: Our star doesn't remain completely still either
articles.body:
Since we were little, we have been taught a fairly simple image of the Solar System: the Sun at the center and the planets revolving around it. An explanation that works perfectly for understanding the basics, but which, when looked at in a little more detail, has a small nuance that may surprise more than one person.

Although its enormous size and mass make the movement virtually imperceptible, our star also moves . The reason lies in something as simple as gravity: the planets not only receive the Sun’s influence, but they themselves also exert a force on it.

"The key lies in the barycenter

To understand this, we need to talk about the so-called barycenter, which is, simply put, the point around which a system made up of two bodies that are gravitationally related moves.

In the case of the Earth and the Sun, that point is very close to the center of our star. It could not be otherwise, considering the enormous difference in mass between the two. That is why, at first glance, it seems that the Earth revolves around a completely motionless Sun.

The situation changes when Jupiter appears

The gas giant is so massive that its influence on the Sun is much more evident. In fact, the center of mass between the two can even be located outside the Sun itself. In other words: while Jupiter travels along its orbit, our star also makes a small movement around that point.

It may seem like a detail without much importance, but it has very interesting consequences. In fact, this little ‘wobble’ of the stars is one of the tools astronomers use to find planets that are light-years away and that we cannot even observe directly.

articles.title: The alleged secret code of the Great Pyramid of Giza that could reveal what it was built for
articles.standfirst: A researcher claims that the dimensions of the pyramid conceal mathematical and astronomical relationships
articles.summary: A researcher claims that the dimensions of the pyramid conceal mathematical and astronomical relationships
articles.body:
T he Great Pyramid of Giza has spent more than 4,500 years defying those who try to explain all its secrets . Although the most widely accepted interpretation is that it was built during the reign of Pharaoh Khufu as part of a funerary complex, new research raises a different possibility: that its very dimensions conceal a mathematical system related to the way the ancient Egyptians understood the universe.

"The hypothesis comes from Sefy Levy, an independent researcher who has analyzed different measurements of the structure and its proportions. His conclusion is striking: the pyramid may have been conceived not only as a funerary monument, but also as a physical representation of knowledge related to time, space, and celestial movements.

A pyramid transformed into a huge mathematical code

The method used by Levy starts from known measurements of the Great Pyramid, such as the length of its base and its height. The researcher applies to them fractions used in the mathematics of ancient Egypt and obtains figures that, according to his interpretation, bear similarities to certain astronomical phenomena.

One of the standout results comes close to 27.55 days, a figure very close to the interval between two consecutive lunar perigees, that is, the period between two moments when the Moon reaches its maximum proximity to Earth.

The researcher also finds relationships that, according to his analysis, bear similarities to cycles associated with planets visible from Earth, including Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, and Mars. Added to this are the well-known geometric approximations of some of the pyramid's proportions to the number pi and the golden ratio.

Levy's interpretation goes beyond a simple mathematical coincidence. In his view, the builders may have used the architecture of the pyramid to preserve for thousands of years a representation of their knowledge about the cosmos. The construction would thus be a kind of “stone memory.”

The proposition, however, should be taken with caution. The work has not yet undergone scientific peer review, so its conclusions cannot be considered a proven explanation of the monument's original purpose

articles.title: 'Geraint Lewis, astrophysicist, recounts the chilling chronology of how Earth will be destroyed: "It will be scorched by the Sun"'
articles.standfirst: The scientist explains in Daily Star how our planet will change over the course of billions of years
articles.summary: The scientist explains in Daily Star how our planet will change over the course of billions of years
articles.body:
P Thinking about the end of the Earth usually leads to imagining immediate scenarios, but astronomy places its disappearance on a completely different timescale. Astrophysicist Geraint Lewis has explained how the universe will evolve and what the fate of our planet will be when the Sun reaches the end of its life .

The sequence will continue for billions of years and will be marked by enormous cosmic transformations. Some will directly affect the Solar System, while others will completely change the appearance of the universe long after the Earth has ceased to exist.

Professor Lewis is clear: “The Earth will be scorched by the expanding Sun”

One of the major anticipated events will be the transformation of the Sun. The star will progressively run out of the fuel it uses to produce energy and, when that time comes, it will begin to change radically.

The Sun will increase in size until it becomes a red giant. Its expansion will cause the closest planets to be exposed to extreme temperatures and, eventually, it will also affect Earth. Lewis sums up the fate of our planet with a blunt phrase: “ It will be scorched by the Sun”.

'Professor Lewis has stated that “the burning of helium in the Sun will cause it to expand and, in about three billion years, the Earth will be scorched by the expanding Sun. It will swallow Mercury, then Venus, and finally Earth" .'

Before reaching that point, humanity would have had to disappear or have found some way to leave Earth. The Earth's surface would cease to be compatible with life long before the Sun reached its maximum expansion.

Much later, the universe will enter an increasingly darker stage. Star formation will decrease until it virtually disappears, and the existing stars will eventually exhaust their fuel.

The final scenario described by Lewis extends over unimaginable periods of time. Earth will be only a remote memory and, eventually, the last stars will also go out, leaving an increasingly colder, darker and emptier universe.

articles.title: The first Neanderthal discovery sparked some truly wild theories
articles.standfirst: The confusion began even before the famous Neander Valley discovery in Germany
articles.summary: The confusion began even before the famous Neander Valley discovery in Germany
articles.body:
Imagine discovering a set of ancient bones unlike anything anyone had seen before, then deciding they belonged to a cave bear, a sickly human, or even a wandering soldier fleeing a war. That may sound absurd today, but when the first Neanderthal remains were uncovered during the 19th century, scientists and ordinary people alike struggled to understand what they were looking at.

Long before Neanderthals became one of the most recognizable branches of the human family tree, their fossils sparked fierce debates, bizarre theories, and some surprisingly imaginative explanations.

The confusion began even before the famous Neander Valley discovery in Germany. In fact, the earliest known Neanderthal fossil was unearthed in Belgium in 1829. Yet researchers at the time failed to recognize its significance. The skull, which belonged to a young child, would not be formally identified as an archaic human relative until 1936, more than a century later.

A second specimen surfaced in Gibraltar in 1848, but it too was largely overlooked. It wasn't until 1856, when quarry workers uncovered unusual bones in Germany's Neander Valley, that the scientific world was forced to confront a difficult question: what exactly were these strange remains?

A far more intriguing conclusion

The workers who discovered the skeleton offered the first explanation, though it was hardly scientific. Believing the bones belonged to a cave bear, they tossed many of them down to the quarry floor. Several fragments were damaged or lost before anyone realized their potential importance.

Fortunately, local schoolteacher Johann Carl Fuhlrott examined the surviving remains and reached a far more intriguing conclusion. He proposed that the bones belonged to an ancient human who had lived in Europe long before recorded history. Today, that idea sounds relatively reasonable, but in the mid-19th century it was remarkably bold.

Fuhlrott's theory arrived two years before Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species, at a time when the concept of human evolution had yet to gain widespread acceptance. Suggesting that humanity might have ancient predecessors was enough to trigger skepticism across much of the scientific community.

The pushback came quickly

Among the loudest critics was German anatomist August Franz Josef Karl Mayer, who argued that the skeleton was not an ancient human at all. Instead, he claimed it belonged to a "Mongolian Cossack " who had supposedly wandered into the cave after being displaced by Russian military campaigns in 1814.

Mayer's explanation only became more elaborate from there. According to his theory, the skeleton's bowed legs were the result of spending years riding horses, while the unusual shape of the skull could be explained by disease and physical deformities.

As far-fetched as that sounds today, Mayer was not alone. Influential German pathologist Rudolf Virchow also rejected the notion of an extinct human species. He insisted that the Neander Valley bones belonged to a modern human whose skeletal features had been distorted by ailments such as rickets and osteoarthritis.

The debate reflected a broader struggle taking place throughout Europe. The idea that humanity might have ancient relatives challenged long-held assumptions about human origins, and many scholars were reluctant to embrace such a revolutionary concept.

Classification deepened divisions within European scientific circles

Not everyone shared that resistance. British biologist Thomas Huxley, one of Darwin's strongest defenders , rejected Mayer's theories and argued that the fossil represented something far more significant. His support helped legitimize the growing belief that the remains belonged to a distinct form of ancient human.

The turning point came in 1864 when Irish geologist William King formally assigned the fossil to a new species: Homo neanderthalensis. Even then, acceptance was far from immediate. The classification deepened divisions within European scientific circles, with some researchers embracing the evidence and others continuing to search for alternative explanations.

Over time, however, additional discoveries made the case impossible to ignore. Fossils found across Europe and western Asia revealed that Neanderthals were not diseased modern humans or lost soldiers, but members of a separate human species that had thrived for hundreds of thousands of years.

Today, Neanderthals occupy a central place in our understanding of human evolution. Scientists know they made tools, hunted large animals, cared for members of their communities, and even interbred with the ancestors of many modern humans.

articles.title: The Great Pyramid may have hidden the secret of its construction inside its own walls
articles.standfirst: A computer model suggests Egyptian workers used rising ramps that disappeared as the monument grew
articles.summary: A computer model suggests Egyptian workers used rising ramps that disappeared as the monument grew
articles.body:
For more than 4,500 years, the Great Pyramid of Giza has concealed one of history’s most persistent mysteries: how ancient Egyptian workers moved and positioned approximately 2.3 million stone blocks without modern cranes, iron tools or heavy-wheeled transportation.

A new study proposes that the answer was built directly into the pyramid. Computer scientist Vicente Luis Rosell Roig developed a model in which workers used several ramps integrated along the monument’s edges, creating rising paths that advanced as each new layer of limestone was completed.

Instead of constructing one enormous external ramp which would have required a vast amount of material the builders could have pulled individual blocks on sledges around the pyramid’s perimeter. Once a section was finished, the ramp would be filled in and effectively disappear inside the completed structure.

Computer simulations recreate the pyramid’s construction

The simulations indicate that this system could have allowed workers to position one block every four to six minutes. Under ideal conditions, the pyramid’s main structure could have been completed in approximately 14 to 21 years. After including quarrying, transportation along the Nile, seasonal interruptions and rest periods, the estimate increases to between 20 and 27 years.

The model is also consistent with some of the unexplained spaces detected inside the Great Pyramid through cosmic-ray muon scans. Researchers discovered a large void above the Grand Gallery in 2017, although its purpose remains unknown. Rosell Roig suggests that such spaces could be remnants of the construction system, but the connection has not been proven.

The study does not definitively solve the mystery. It presents a testable engineering explanation, not direct archaeological evidence that the ramps existed. Future inspections would need to uncover specific signs, including unusual filling patterns near the pyramid’s edges or wear around its corners, before scientists could confirm that the ancient builders really used this method.

articles.title: Immanuel Kant, philosopher, "Rules for Happiness: something to do, someone to love, something to hope for"
articles.standfirst: The famous three-part formula for a fulfilling life is widely attributed to Kant, although the historical record points elsewhere
articles.summary: The famous three-part formula for a fulfilling life is widely attributed to Kant, although the historical record points elsewhere
articles.body:
Few ideas about happiness are as concise as the famous formula attributed to Immanuel Kant : “Rules for Happiness: something to do, someone to love, something to hope for.”

The quotation has circulated widely online, appearing on collections of philosophical sayings and motivational websites. Goodreads lists it under Kant's name, while Play For Thoughts also includes it among its collection of philosophical reflections on happiness.

Yet there is an important historical qualification. Goodreads itself notes that its quotations are community-submitted and not verified. More detailed research into the wording has found no known work by Kant containing the sentence.

Instead, the closest documented source is George Washington Burnap , a 19th-century American clergyman who published a remarkably similar formulation in The Sphere and Duties of Woman: A Course of Lectures in 1848.

Burnap wrote: "The grand essentials to happiness in this life are something to do, something to love, and something to hope for."

The line has subsequently been attributed to several different figures, including Kant and Joseph Addison , helping explain why it remains attached to famous names across the internet.

That does not make the sentiment irrelevant to Kant's philosophy. In fact, the relationship between happiness, morality and hope was an important part of Kant's thinking, although his position was considerably more sophisticated than the three-part maxim suggests.

Kant's philosophy saw happiness as more complicated than a simple formula

Immanuel Kant , born in Königsberg in 1724, became one of the most influential philosophers of the modern era.

His work transformed discussions of knowledge, ethics, reason and human freedom. The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy identifies human autonomy as a central feature of his critical philosophy, particularly the idea that practical reason gives itself the moral law.

For Kant , happiness was something human beings naturally sought, but it could not simply serve as the foundation of morality.

He argued that people have different desires and ideas about what would make them happy, meaning that happiness is too indeterminate to provide a universal moral rule.

This distinction is crucial. Kant did not argue that happiness was unimportant. Rather, he separated the desire to be happy from the question of how a person ought to behave.

His concept of the "highest good" brought morality and happiness together. Kant argued that virtue and happiness should ultimately coexist, with happiness understood as appropriate to moral worth.

The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy describes this as an ideal combining virtue with happiness rather than treating pleasure or satisfaction as the sole measure of a good life.

Hope was also especially significant in Kant's philosophy. The Stanford Encyclopedia notes that Kant treated "What may I hope?" as one of philosophy's fundamental questions, alongside questions about what humans can know and what they ought to do.

That makes the final element of the famous three-part quotation particularly interesting. Although the exact wording is apparently not Kant's , hope genuinely occupied an important position in his philosophical system.

The three ideas also remain compelling because they describe different dimensions of ordinary life. "Something to do" suggests purpose and activity.

"Someone to love" points toward relationships and connection. "Something to hope for" introduces a future-oriented element, giving people something beyond the present moment toward which they can direct their expectations.

The enduring appeal of the quotation may therefore have less to do with Kant himself than with the simplicity of the formula.

It does not promise that happiness comes from wealth, fame or constant pleasure. Instead, it describes a life containing activity, meaningful relationships and an expectation of something still to come.

At the same time, readers should be careful when presenting the sentence as a direct Kant quotation. Multiple sources now identify Burnap as the likely original author, and scholarly discussions have highlighted the attribution problem.

So while the headline attribution remains popular, the historical evidence tells a more complicated story.

Kant undoubtedly wrote extensively about happiness and hope, but the memorable three-part rule appears to have acquired his name long after the words were first published.

Whether credited to Kant or understood through Burnap's original formulation, however, the basic idea has survived because it offers an unusually accessible way to think about a fulfilling life: purpose in the present, meaningful human connection and something worth looking toward in the future.

Whether credited to Kant or understood through Burnap's original formulation, however, the basic idea has survived because it offers an unusually accessible way to think about a fulfilling life: purpose in the present, meaningful human connection and something worth looking toward in the future.

articles.title: The paradigm of the brain changes completely after the discovery by a group of scientists: it consists of two separate organs that have been fused
articles.standfirst: A group of experts from Stanford University believes that our understanding of this part of our body has always been wrong
articles.summary: A group of experts from Stanford University believes that our understanding of this part of our body has always been wrong
articles.body:
As of 2026, research on human organs continues to leave scientists speechless. A group of experts from Stanford University began observing the brain and came to the conclusion that it is not a simple organ. We could be talking about two separate organs that have been fused.

If this paradigm is indeed confirmed, research into diseases that weaken motor neurons would open up a new avenue of study. What this group of scientists points out is that at one stage of our evolution, the brain was divided into the hindbrain and the upper brain (forebrain and midbrain).

The brain developed as two well-differentiated organs that eventually joined together

Both parts had different functions. The rhombencephalon was responsible for everything related to the automatic functions that keep us alive, that is, breathing, sleep, or heart rate. For its part, the other organ would be in charge of language, consciousness, and abstract reasoning. However, over time, both parts merged into one and formed the organ we have today.

The key is that both parts were supposed to develop together, but they function properly once they have joined. Kyle Loh, one of the study's authors, explains how his finding originated in remarks reported by Daily Mail: “We have demonstrated for the first time that the front part of the brain originates from a progenitor cell that is completely different from that of the back part of the brain”.

From this discovery onward, the door to investigating diseases such as ALS or muscular atrophy is completely open. This is explained by Rayyan Jokhai, another of the authors: “We now have a model to better understand these devastating diseases and work on the development of regenerative therapies to combat them.”

articles.title: Confucius, Chinese philosopher: "It does not matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop"
articles.standfirst: Slow progress may feel frustrating, but the philosopher’s message suggests that consistency matters more than pace
articles.summary: Slow progress may feel frustrating, but the philosopher’s message suggests that consistency matters more than pace
articles.body:
There is a particular kind of frustration that comes from making progress too slowly. A goal can still be getting closer, yet it may not feel that way when someone else appears to be advancing faster, achieving more or reaching milestones sooner.

That is what gives one of the best-known quotes attributed to Confucius its staying power: “It does not matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop.”

The message isn't really about speed at all. It's about endurance. Progress is often measured by visible outcomes, but the harder part usually happens before those results appear.

Learning, recovering, rebuilding and improving can all involve long stretches where very little seems to change from one day to the next. That doesn't mean nothing is happening.

Danger of comparing your pace with someone else

One of the easiest ways to lose momentum is to measure your progress against another person’s timeline. Careers rarely develop at the same speed. Neither do relationships, finances, education or personal growth.

Someone may reach a goal quickly because they began with different advantages, fewer obstacles or simply better timing. Another person may take longer and still end up in the same place.

The quote attributed to Confucius cuts through that comparison by shifting the focus back to the individual journey. That idea turns persistence into the real measure of progress.

Moving slowly can be more sustainable

Fast progress can be exciting, but it isn't always durable. Intense bursts of effort are difficult to maintain indefinitely. Slow, repeatable habits are often less impressive in the short term but far more powerful over months or years.

A person who reads a few pages every day can finish dozens of books. Someone who saves a small amount consistently can gradually build security. An athlete who improves one weakness at a time can eventually transform performance.

None of those changes needs to happen quickly to matter. Consistency creates momentum precisely because it can survive ordinary life.

Stopping and resting not the same thing

The quote can also be misunderstood. People need breaks. Illness, exhaustion, disappointment and changing circumstances can require someone to slow down or pause entirely. A pause doesn't have to mean surrender.

The important distinction is whether the goal has been abandoned or simply approached differently. Sometimes persistence looks like pushing forward. Other times it means recovering enough to begin again.

That's why the quote remains useful centuries after the philosophy associated with Confucius first emerged. It rejects the idea that success belongs only to the fastest. Progress can be uneven, quiet and frustratingly slow. It still counts.

articles.title: Science provided advance information about the end of civilization What will happen on November 13, 2026?
articles.standfirst: Scientists have predicted that the end of the world is approaching, with the end of civilization projected before the end of 2026.
articles.summary: Scientists have predicted that the end of the world is approaching, with the end of civilization projected before the end of 2026.
articles.body:
"Heinz von Foerster, considered one of the fathers of cybernetics, made very profound warnings about Artificial Intelligence in an interview given in 1995 to the organization The Information Philosopher .

His reflections are surprising today because they accurately anticipated the psychological and ethical problems we are experiencing with modern AI.

The 1960 prediction that extends to November 2026

November 13, 2026 was not presented by scientists as a literal date for the end of humanity.

A scientific study published in 1960 is once again drawing attention by placing on November 13, 2026 a deadline associated with the growth of the world population, indicating that it would grow at an increasingly accelerated rate. Among its authors was Heinz von Foerster, a researcher specializing in cybernetics, whose work also left warnings about artificial intelligence that today seem especially relevant.

The calculation did not literally establish that humanity would disappear that day. The work, published in Science, proposed that, if population growth maintained the trend observed during the previous two millennia, the figure would mathematically approach infinity in November 2026. Demographic reality, however, took a different path.

When von Foerster, Patricia M. Mora, and Lawrence W. Amiot published that study, the world population was around 3 billion people. Their model was based on an acceleration of growth that, extrapolated unchanged, led to a mathematical singularity in November 2026 , at which point the population would tend toward infinity.

More than six decades later, the world's population is very far from that scenario. The UN estimates that there were 8.2 billion inhabitants in 2024 and projects that it will reach around 10.3 billion by the mid-2080s , before beginning a gradual decline.

The difference between that calculation and current projections has to do, among other factors, with the decline in fertility. The UN points out that birth rates have fallen more than expected in some of the most populous countries, especially in China, significantly altering the forecasts made decades earlier.

Von Foerster's name has returned to the conversation for another reason. In an interview given in 1995 to The Information Philosopher, the scientist spoke about artificial intelligence and questioned the tendency to attribute human abilities to machines simply because they were capable of carrying out certain tasks.

Their key predictions are summarized in three points:

1. The "dangerous" illusion that machines think like humans Von Foerster described it as "dangerous" to assume that machines think, reason, or behave according to human standards. He warned that, even if technology were to advance to the point of being extremely intelligent, logical intelligence is not equivalent to possessing morality, consciousness, values, or human emotions.

2. Emotional dependency and chatbots. His most accurate prediction was social in nature. He warned about the risk of humanity developing a bond of emotional dependency toward machines, assuming human-type interactions with them. Decades later, this has come true to the letter with the rise of AI chatbots, with which many people seek emotional connections or even enter into romantic relationships.

3. "Trivial machines" and the loss of critical thinking. As an expert in cybernetics, Von Foerster was concerned that the real danger was not that machines would become human, but the opposite: that humans would become like machines. He introduced the concept of "trivial machines" (systems that, when given an input X, always produce a predictable response Y). He warned that if society relied blindly on technology to obtain automated answers, people would lose their critical thinking, their creativity, and their capacity for ethical choice , "trivializing" themselves.

This is not the first time that apocalyptic predictions have emerged, but this particular study has received significant attention due to its foundation in solid, contemporary scientific analysis.

What will happen on November 13, 2026

The scientist's stance was not that of a science fiction alarmist fearing a rebellion of destructive robots. Instead, he left a humanistic warning: the danger of AI is not its technical capability, but our tendency to delegate to it the responsibility and values that belong only to us humans.

Its argument is especially recognizable in the era of AI models capable of holding conversations, generating texts, and answering questions in natural language.

Contrary to what the formula of the last century assumed, the global birth rate has fallen drastically.

Nothing in current demographic projections indicates that that date will mark the end of civilization. The 1960 model stopped describing the actual evolution of the population long before reaching its mathematical singularity.

On November 13, 2026, therefore, it will arrive without the world’s population approaching infinity. The date will be, above all, the endpoint of a mathematical extrapolation published in 1960 and an opportunity to remember why a formula that works on past data does not necessarily describe the future.

articles.title: Confucius, philosopher: "If you already know what you have to do and you do not do it, then you are worse off than before"
articles.standfirst: Respect and ethics in governance can help us combat current corruption, especially in the face of citizens' distrust, through Confucius's reflection on good conduct.
articles.summary: Respect and ethics in governance can help us combat current corruption, especially in the face of citizens' distrust, through Confucius's reflection on good conduct.
articles.body:
"Confucius, through his work the Analects, offers us a critical view of human conduct, emphasizing respect and morality in relationships . His famous quote “If you already know what you have to do and you do not do it, then you are worse off than before” resonates in an era dominated by work pressure and hyperproductivity, where many struggle to meet unattainable expectations. This moral dilemma, heightened by uncertainty and the speed of everyday life, confronts us with the need to reflect on our actions and values.

In a contemporary context marked by individualism and consumerism, Confucian philosophy proposes a return to ethics and governance based on respect. The dilemma of acting with integrity in an environment full of stimuli and social comparisons highlights the relevance of Confucius's teachings. The ability to address these problems from an ethical perspective is essential in the pursuit of more harmonious and meaningful relationships in our daily lives.

If you already know what you have to do and you don't do it, then you are worse off than before

The philosophy of Confucius and his legacy in ethics and governance

Confucius, known as Kǒng Qiū, was a Chinese philosopher born in 551 BC in the state of Lu and died in 479 BC. He is known as the founder of Confucianism , a school of thought that highlights the importance of human relationships and ethics in governance. His impact on culture and society has endured for more than 2,000 years, making him a key reference on how to achieve good government based on virtue and morality.

Confucius's thought emphasizes benevolence, justice, loyalty, and respect for social hierarchy . Unlike other philosophical currents, such as Legalism, which focuses on control and strict rules, Confucius proposed an ethic centered on morality as the foundation for a harmonious society. Like Lao-Tzu, Confucius advocated benevolence and harmony, reflecting a shared pursuit of wisdom in their respective philosophies. Through his most influential work, "The Analects," he compiled teachings that underscore the importance of education and respect in cultivating healthy interpersonal relationships.

articles.title: 'Demosthenes, philosopher: "Among our calculations, the most dangerous are those we call illusions"'
articles.standfirst: An interesting reflection on expectations and reality
articles.summary: An interesting reflection on expectations and reality
articles.body:
Life is full of complex moments and challenges that one must overcome. Hope can be an important factor in facing such situations, but one must be careful and know how to draw the line between reason and illusion , since the perception of reality can be altered. A line of thought shared by Demosthenes , one of the best-known philosophers in history.

He who was an Athenian orator and politician of ancient Greece , among his many notable phrases, once said: “Among our calculations, the most dangerous are those we call illusions.” A phrase with which he establishes the internal debate between reason and illusion.

Self-deception and the false perception of optimism

In this reflection, Demosthenes sets out a clear and direct warning about the fact that important decisions are based on unrealistic desires , on illusions and false hopes. The best method, according to the philosopher, is for your way of acting to adhere to reality, without expectations that go beyond what is normal.

Self-deception, according to the Greek philosopher, is one of the obstacles a person may face, since it can cause one to lose sight of what one has before them and of what is most likely to happen. In fact, in his work ‘Olynthiacs’, he already spoke about this: “ Nothing is as easy as deceiving oneself ; for what each man desires, that is what he believes to be true”.

According to Demosthenes' idea, when the variable of illusion is introduced into a calculation, logic, strategy, and foresight are lost. All reason is lost because of a sensitive and subjective factor that does not always provide a valid and real explanation for what is around us. Thinking that certain things will happen out of pure optimism is a problem when reality strikes and shows another side of life.

articles.title: Madeleine McCann case: Christian Brueckner reveals what he was doing 137 meters from the scene. "He was selling drugs"
articles.standfirst: The main suspect in the case claims that on that night he was on a beach in Praia da Luz selling marijuana and that the Portuguese Police even detained him up to three times.
articles.summary: The main suspect in the case claims that on that night he was on a beach in Praia da Luz selling marijuana and that the Portuguese Police even detained him up to three times.
articles.body:
Christian Brueckner, the main suspect in the disappearance of Madeleine McCann , has described in detail for the first time what he was doing in Praia da Luz on the night of May 3, 2007.

In his statements, he claims that he was about 137 meters from the place where the girl's family was staying and denies having had any involvement in her disappearance.

The German maintains that he had arrived from Spain with marijuana that he brought into Portugal and that he tried to leave the area when police checks were activated after Madeleine's disappearance was confirmed.

Brueckner claims that the Police arrested him three times

According to his version, the Portuguese agents stopped him as many as three times while they were searching for the girl . He says he was traveling in a van loaded with narcotics, but the police did not find the drugs and he was able to continue on his way.

Brueckner also explains that he kept silent for years because, he claims, he feared that the authorities would try to incriminate him for the disappearance. The public disclosure of this version comes after, in the past, he had refused to cooperate with British investigators.

The investigation into Madeleine began on May 3, 2007 , when the three-year-old girl disappeared from the apartment where she was staying with her parents at the Ocean Club complex in Praia da Luz. Her parents were having dinner at a nearby restaurant when the disappearance occurred.

He remains the prime suspect

German authorities publicly identified Brueckner as the main suspect in 2020 and maintain the theory that Madeleine died after being abducted. However, he has never been formally charged over the girl's disappearance, and he continues to deny any involvement in the case.

His connection to Praia da Luz dated back earlier: he lived for years in the Algarve and served a seven-year sentence for the rape of a 72-year-old woman committed in the town in 2005, two years before Madeleine's disappearance. He was released in September 2025 and remains under investigation in the McCann case.

Brueckner is now preparing an autobiography in which he plans to defend his innocence and set out his own version of events . The investigation remains open nearly two decades later : the United Kingdom, Germany and Portugal are pursuing different lines of inquiry in search of evidence to clarify what happened that night.

articles.title: Stonehenge: one of history’s best kept secrets
articles.standfirst: For thousands of years, the mystery has remained standing
articles.summary: For thousands of years, the mystery has remained standing
articles.body:
It seems as if history itself wanted to hide the true story behind one of the most famous archaeological sites on the planet. Stonehenge remains one of history’s greatest enigmas, with multiple theories surrounding its purpose, construction and the people who built it . The debate could continue for as long as the stones have stood on Salisbury Plain.

Located in southern England, Stonehenge was built by ancient Britons around 4,600 years ago, but those who created it left no written records explaining what the monument was meant to represent . That absence has allowed different theories and legends to grow around the site over the centuries. National Geographic notes that Stonehenge has been linked to everything from Druids and Romans to the legend of Merlin .

According to Arthurian folklore, the monument was created by Merlin, the legendary wizard associated with King Arthur. The story claims that Merlin magically transported the massive stones from Ireland, where giants had supposedly assembled them.

A monument built over centuries

Archaeological research has changed much of what was once believed about Stonehenge. The monument was not built all at once. Its construction began around 5,000 years ago with a circular earthwork before later stages introduced the massive stones that define the site today.

Inside the circle are five trilithons, each formed by two standing stones with a large lintel placed across the top, creating a horseshoe-shaped arrangement. Around 2600 B.C., about 80 bluestones from Wales were incorporated into the monument and rearranged several times. Centuries later, larger sarsen stones were added, with some weighing around 25 tons and transported roughly 19 miles to Salisbury Plain. It has been estimated that constructing Stonehenge required well over 20 million hours of work.

Chemical analysis has also traced the Altar Stone, the largest of the non-sarsen stones, to Scotland, around 466 miles away. The distance traveled by some of the stones remains one of the questions surrounding how prehistoric communities were able to build the monument.

The purpose remains the biggest question

The reason Stonehenge was built is still debated . Some interpretations connect the monument to religious ceremonies, while others focus on its relationship with the sun, moon and astronomical events. Its alignment with the summer and winter solstices has led researchers to consider whether the site was used to follow seasonal changes or as a form of ancient calendar.

Other theories point toward healing or ancestor worship. Research led by archaeologist Mike Parker Pearson has connected Stonehenge with nearby Durrington Walls and suggested that the two sites represented different domains, with Stonehenge associated with the dead and the wooden circle with the living. Evidence of cremated human remains also supports the idea that the area had an important connection with death and ritual.

Part of a much larger landscape

Stonehenge was also part of a much larger prehistoric landscape that included avenues, settlements and burial sites . Archaeological work has shown that people traveled from different parts of Britain to the area, suggesting the monument attracted communities from far beyond Salisbury Plain. That is what makes Stonehenge so difficult to define. articles.title: Winston Churchill, Prime Minister of the United Kingdom: “There is a terrible amount of lies about the world, and the worst thing is that half of them are true”
articles.standfirst: Attributed to the historic British leader who, decades later, still fits a very current problem
articles.summary: Attributed to the historic British leader who, decades later, still fits a very current problem
articles.body:
There are phrases that outlive the person who uttered them or to whom they are attributed because, over time, they still have something to say. This is the case with one of the reflections circulating associated with Winston Churchill , which focuses on a question as old as politics itself: to what extent can we be sure that what we hear or read is true.

This reflection is especially striking when placed in the context of the era Churchill lived through. The British politician led the Government during some of the most difficult moments of the 20th century , with the Second World War as the main setting and with propaganda playing a fundamental role.

"Winston Churchill: “The worst thing is that half of them are true”

“There is a terrible amount of lies about the world, and the worst thing is that half of them are true ”. The phrase plays with a simple but uncomfortable idea: it is not always easy to separate a complete lie from information that mixes real facts , half-truths, and invented elements.

In those years, information was also a tool of power. Governments spread certain messages to maintain the population's morale, influence their citizens, or weaken the enemy. The press, radio, and political speeches were essential in shaping the image of what was happening.

Churchill , in addition to being a politician, was a writer and one of the great orators of his time. His ability to turn certain ideas into easy-to-remember phrases helped create a public image that has endured to this day.

That said, it is worth adding a small asterisk to the quote. As happens with many sayings attributed to historical figures, it is not always easy to find a primary source that allows us to confirm with absolute certainty exactly when he spoke those words. Over the years, some quotes change slightly or end up being associated with figures who never said them.

But the essence of the reflection remains recognizable. In an era in which any information can be spread in a matter of seconds, the problem does not consist solely in detecting an obvious lie . Sometimes , what is truly complicated is discovering how much truth there is within it.

articles.title: Julio Cortázar, Argentine writer: “I don’t renounce anything, I simply do what I can so that things renounce me”
articles.standfirst: The search for identity in a changing world can find answers in the literary legacy of Julio Cortázar, who through his work explores the complexity of being human.
articles.summary: The search for identity in a changing world can find answers in the literary legacy of Julio Cortázar, who through his work explores the complexity of being human.
articles.body:
'J ulio Cortázar , a key figure in contemporary literature, explores in his work "Hopscotch" the search for meaning in a chaotic world . The quote “I renounce nothing; I simply do what I can so that things renounce me” reflects an inner struggle that still resonates today in a context of hyperconnectivity and social pressure. In the age of social media, many feel that their lives lack direction, dragged along by others’ expectations and the constant bombardment of stimuli.'

Individualism and the speed of everyday life amplify feelings of uncertainty. This situation is manifested in the difficulty of being alone and the need for validation, problems that Cortázar addresses through characters who navigate their own search for authenticity . In a world where social comparison is the order of the day, his work invites reflection on creative freedom and the true meaning of happiness.

I renounce nothing, I simply do what I can so that things renounce me

The Literary Legacy of Julio Cortázar

'Julio Cortázar (1914-1984) was an Argentine writer who stood out for his innovative approach and his ability to intertwine the real with the fantastic . He was born in Brussels and grew up in Argentina, where he began his literary career. Cortázar became one of the most relevant figures of the Latin American "boom," which included authors such as Gabriel García Márquez and Mario Vargas Llosa. With works such as "Hopscotch," the author transformed Hispanic narrative and left a legacy that continues to resonate in contemporary literature.'

Cortázar's thought is deeply linked to his political commitment and to his search for new forms of expression. He used elements of magical realism and surrealism to explore human experience and the complexity of identity. Through his activism, especially during the military dictatorship in Argentina, he reflected in his writing a critique of oppression and a search for freedom. His style has influenced numerous contemporary authors, and his work continues to be a reference point in modern literature.

articles.title: 'George Clooney told Presley Gerber "I’m here for you" weeks before his death'
articles.standfirst: Sources close to the actor say that he maintained a close relationship with Cindy Crawford's son for years, including reaching out after his 2018 arrest for drunk driving.
articles.summary: Sources close to the actor say that he maintained a close relationship with Cindy Crawford's son for years, including reaching out after his 2018 arrest for drunk driving.
articles.body:
P resley Gerber , son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, died last Sunday at the age of 27 from a suspected overdose, as confirmed by the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner's Office. Gerber died at the Resolutions Living facility, a rehabilitation center in Santa Monica valued at $7.7 million.

George Clooney, Rande Gerber's partner in the Casamigos tequila company and whom Presley and his sister Kaia called "Uncle George", sent him messages of support in recent times, according to a source cited by the Daily Mail . "Recently, George shared affectionate notes like "I'm here for you," that kind of thing," the source said.

A bond built over years of friendship

Sources close to the actor say that he maintained a close relationship with Cindy Crawford's son for years, including a warning after his 2018 arrest for drunk driving.

A person close to Amal Clooney described the bond between the two as close: " Presley was more than a friend's son. They had a bond" , she told the Daily Mail.

A constant message: stay clean

'According to someone close to Clooney, the advice the actor kept repeating to Presley was simple: stay clean, drawing on his own experience. Clooney admitted in October 2025 to having tried drugs in the past, although he insisted it had never been a serious problem for him. "He was never addicted, but he tried it and knows the pull of drugs, so he could speak openly with Presley about this and Presley could relate", the source explained.'

'The news of Presley's death hit Clooney's circle hard. "George is devastated by this because Rande is his best friend and everyone was fond of Presley", a source told the Daily Mail.'

The Crawford-Gerber family requested privacy in a joint statement after confirming the death. According to a source cited by Page Six, Presley had entered the rehabilitation center just a few days before dying because "he knew he needed help", although he did not appear sober when he arrived.

articles.title: Lao-Tzu, Chinese philosopher: "He who obtains has no peace; he who gives finds joy"
articles.standfirst: The search for an authentic life can find echoes in the philosophy of Lao-Tzu, who proposes that living in harmony with the Tao guides us in facing everyday dissatisfaction.
articles.summary: The search for an authentic life can find echoes in the philosophy of Lao-Tzu, who proposes that living in harmony with the Tao guides us in facing everyday dissatisfaction.
articles.body:
"In a world where the pursuit of happiness becomes a constant labyrinth, many feel trapped in the need to obtain , to accumulate, believing that this will bring them peace. However, it is in this striving that deep frustration and loneliness arise, resulting in a cycle of dissatisfaction. The experience that obtaining brings nothing but emptiness leaves the human being in a state of restlessness. The pressure for others' approval intertwines with the fear of making mistakes, increasingly complicating the direction of our lives.

Lao-Tzu's work "Tao Te Ching" suggests that true joy lies in the act of giving. This reflection invites us to reconsider our human nature: by giving, we find meaning and connection, transforming the self-centered pursuit into an experience of fulfillment and inner peace. By adopting this perspective, the challenge of living in a world that prioritizes acquisition over generosity is revealed, outlining a path toward personal and emotional balance .

He who obtains has no peace. He who gives finds joy.

The philosophy of Lao-Tzu and his teachings on action and harmony

Lao-Tzu, also known as Lao Tzu, is a Chinese philosopher traditionally regarded as the founder of Taoism , a school of thought that has endured throughout history. His figure is enigmatic, and his historical existence is a matter of debate, with some scholars suggesting that he may be more myth than reality. He is credited with the authorship of the "Tao Te Ching," a fundamental work that encompasses themes such as individual spirituality and practices of governance, thus marking a milestone in Chinese and world philosophy.

Lao-Tse's thought is expressed in concepts such as the "Tao," which symbolizes the universal way and harmony with nature, and "wei-wu-wei," which refers to action through inaction . These ideas contrast with those of his contemporary Confucius, who emphasized morality and the rigidity of rituals. Furthermore, the duality of yin and yang, present in his work, resonates with other Eastern thinkers, highlighting the need for balance in life. Lao-Tse invites reflection on the place of the human being in the cosmos, proposing a constant search for harmony and connection with one's surroundings.

articles.title: George Eliot, writer: "It is never too late to be what you might have been"
articles.standfirst: George Eliot and the mystery of an enduring quote
articles.summary: George Eliot and the mystery of an enduring quote
articles.body:
The words “It is never too late to be what you might have been” are among the most recognizable quotations associated with George Eliot .

Yet there’s an important problem with the attribution: researchers haven’t found the sentence in Eliot’s novels, letters, or other known writings.

Quote Investigator traces the earliest known appearance of the wording to an 1881 issue of Literary News, where it was submitted by a reader as part of a collection of supposed “gems” from Eliot . The quotation was printed without a source, and there’s no evidence that Eliot actually wrote or said it.

That mystery is interesting because the sentiment fits Eliot’s reputation as a writer concerned with moral choices and experience.

Born Mary Ann Evans in Warwickshire in 1819, she later moved to London, worked at the Westminster Review and became an intellectual before turning to fiction. She adopted the name George Eliot when her first novel, Adam Bede, appeared in 1859.

Her novels rejected romantic conventions and focused on ordinary people, relationships and difficult social realities. Works including The Mill on the Floss, Silas Marner and Middlemarch established her as a novelist of the Victorian era.

The novelist behind the famous words

Middlemarch, published in installments during 1871 and 1872, is an example of Eliot’s interest in ambition and unrealized potential. Its physician, Tertius Lydgate, is portrayed as an educated reformer determined to modernize medical practice.

Eliot’s own life involved choices that challenged Victorian expectations. Her long partnership with philosopher and critic George Henry Lewes defied social rules, while her career demonstrated how far she could move beyond the world in which she was raised. After Lewes died in 1878, she married John Cross in 1880, but died that year at age 61.

The famous quotation, then, may not belong to George Eliot . Quote Investigator suggests it may have evolved from Adelaide Anne Procter’s 1859 poem “A Legend of Provence,” which includes the line, “We always may be what we might have been.”

Even if the wording isn’t Eliot’s , the words reflect a question that runs through her fiction over how much of a life is shaped by choices and circumstances.
